result:
I played all 24 months. The final net cost is **$887.98M**. All three training runs were met, there were no penalties, and no inference demand went unserved.

| Window | Done / needed (kH-months) |
|---|---|
| Months 0–7 | 94.2 / 60 |
| Months 8–15 | 265.9 / 140 |
| Months 16–23 | about 338 / 320 (301.7 going into month 23, which had about 34 spare) |

**Settlement:** total spend was $1,096.6M:
- GPUs: $765M
- Power: $196.5M
- Reserved cloud: $137.1M
- Spot: $10.2M
- Interest: $17.5M
- Resales brought back $29.8M.

On top of that, $67.5M of power obligations after month 23 were charged at settlement. The remaining GPUs were credited at $276.1M of end-of-game value.

**How it went:**
- **Months 0–3:** I bought 24k gen H GPUs (vendor plus broker A) and signed 60 MW of extra power. That brought the fleet to 44k GPUs, which covered windows 2 and 3 cheaply. Spot capacity filled the first window while new power was still coming online.
- **Broker A:** it delivered both orders (2/2), so I relied on it while the vendor's shipments looked slow in month 3.
- **Gen N launch:** the rumours ("around 18", "15", "17") narrowed the launch to month 16 or 17. No confirmation came in month 15, so I reserved 6 kH before the launch. It launched in month 17, and I reserved 10 kH more for months 18–23 at the 25% lower post-launch price. I asked for 12, but providers capped me at 10.
- **Export controls** hit in month 13. Only a small 6k gen H order was still in the queue, and it had already shipped by month 10. Nothing was bought after that, so the controls didn't affect me.
- **Growth** looked like about 4% a month for most of the game and possibly 7% near the end. I planned window 3 for 7% growth and kept a margin of 15–20 kH-months.
- At the end, I sold 4.14k gen H GPUs: some had no power after a power contract expired in month 19, and the rest went in the last month because selling then paid slightly more than holding them to settlement.

**Where it lost money:** window 2 finished with about 126 kH-months more than it needed, because the fleet was sized for the much larger window 3. I could have bought some of those GPUs later to cut cost and interest. Two notes also failed to parse as commands, but nothing was affected: their text had a stray `;` that split it into a separate command.
